Welcome to Ewell Grove Primary & Nursery School
As the Headteacher of Ewell Grove, I am delighted to welcome you to our thriving and vibrant village school. Here, we believe that education goes beyond simply meeting curriculum objectives; it is about developing meaningful relationships that foster a strong sense of community. As children move through our school, from their earliest formative years, we build upon the experiences they have already gained. With our school foundations deeply rooted in Early Years principles, we believe that the curriculum we offer must preserve and cherish the uniqueness of childhood.

pageCache.text:
A Primary Trust for Primary Schools
Maths
Mathematics is an engaging and fun subject. At Ewell Grove, our goal is to help every child build their confidence and skills in order to prepare them for the future. We emphasise a curriculum that enables the children to become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics, developing conceptual understanding and the ability to recall and apply knowledge rapidly and accurately.
We aim for children to appreciate the relevance of mathematics in daily life and its significance in modern Britain. Our teaching approach integrates mathematical skills across various subjects. An understanding of mathematics is regarded as an essential tool for making sense of the world around us. Children need to be able to apply the mathematics they know in a diverse range of situations and contexts with increasing fluency.
Children will be encouraged to reason mathematically by following a line of enquiry, identifying relationships and making connections in order to demonstrate their understanding or proof of a solution to a problem. It is through the application of their mathematical skills that children will be motivated and enthused to develop their mathematical thinking.
In EYFS and KS1, we focus on developing children’s understanding of the five principles of number and place value as outlined in our calculation policy. They will gain competence in the four basic operations (+, -, ×, ÷) through a variety of practical activities. As they grow in confidence, children will learn to recognise and use number bonds, doubles, and halves, which will enhance their efficiency in calculations. We will explore inverse relationships between operations, which serve as a valuable tool for checking calculations and understanding related facts. Children will also be introduced to comparative measures and vocabulary for mass, length, time, and capacity before transitioning to standard units. Furthermore, they will use shape and pattern to investigate the world around them and engage in the exploration of properties through hands-on practical experiences.
In KS2, we will build upon the use of practical apparatus to deepen and consolidate our understanding of concepts such as place value, fractions, and calculations. Their understanding of place value will be essential for performing calculations that involve exchanges and decimals. The children will transition from practical work to formal written methods for addition, subtraction, long multiplication, and division. The foundational work on algebra initiated in EYFS and KS1 will continue to be developed. Children will learn to use standard measures with increasing accuracy for mass, length, time, and capacity, ensuring a comprehensive mathematical education. By engaging with mathematics in a meaningful way, we aim to cultivate a generation of confident, capable learners who can apply their skills in a variety of contexts.

A Primary Trust for Primary Schools
Art
Subjects
Art
At Ewell Grove art is a powerful tool to inspire, engage, and challenge pupils. Creativity and imagination play vital roles in fostering self-awareness and cultivating an appreciation for the world around them. We support children in expressing themselves through art, craft, and design, encouraging them to share their ideas, experiences, and imaginations. Our art curriculum is further enriched by the ‘Kapow’ program, which provides high-quality, creative resources.
Children will learn to compare and contrast the works of inspirational artists from ancient to contemporary times, developing a rich vocabulary for appreciation and description. They will apply techniques from different artworks to interpret existing pieces and to envision their own creative ideas. The significance of art and design in shaping our history and culture will be an essential part of their learning journey. Every child's work will be valued and respected, showcased through displays throughout the school. Emphasising choice, we encourage children to decide how best to represent their ideas, experiences, and imaginations. Children will engage in critiquing their own work and that of their peers, fostering a reflective and collaborative artistic community.
Art is taught daily through focused lessons and independent learning opportunities, reflecting our inclusive and adaptive approach. Children will gain hands-on experience with a variety of media, including drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, and various craft techniques. They will explore and experiment with elements such as colour, form, line, pattern, shape, texture, and tone.
Questioning techniques are used to stimulate idea development and assess understanding of new vocabulary which is taught progressively across the school. During independent learning opportunities, children are provided with visual aids that outline the sequence of steps for each task along with a diverse range of resources for exploration and experimentation. Children develop sketchbooks/art folders as a tool for generating ideas. Sketchbooks/art folders also enable the children to explore, practice and refine their techniques, often building their ideas towards a final piece.
Our art curriculum supports children to articulate their thoughts and expand their vocabulary. They learn to describe their artistic choices and the elements they observe in various works, enhancing their ability to express ideas effectively. Children will develop characteristics of effective learning as they will learn how to use their senses to explore the world around them, engage in open-ended activities and represent experiences through art. They will also develop confidence and resilience to take risks, show persistence and problem solve. Art at Ewell Grove is cross-curricular and will often be linked to high-quality texts which are shared through a range of subjects. Children will feel a sense of pride and achievement through the celebration of their art throughout their time at Ewell Grove.

Opening Worlds
At Ewell Grove we use Opening Worlds for teaching history, geography and religion for Years 3 to 6. Opening Worlds is an exciting knowledge-rich humanities programme which develops speaking, listening and communication skills through the progression of rich vocabulary, questioning and storytelling.
In history, children will use the concepts of continuity and change, cause and consequence, similarity, difference and significance, in order to make connections, draw contrasts, analyse trends, frame historically-valid questions and create their own structured accounts, including written narratives and analyses. They will practise the methods of historical enquiry, understand how evidence is used rigorously to make historical claims, and discern how and why contrasting arguments and interpretations of the past have been constructed.
In geography, children will think about geographical questions using concepts of place, scale, space, distance, interaction and relationships. They will collect, analyse and communicate with a range of data gathered through experiences of fieldwork that deepen their understanding of geographical processes. A range of sources of geographical information will be interpreted, including maps, diagrams, globes, aerial photographs and geographical information systems. Geographical information will be communicated in a variety of ways, including through maps, numerical and quantitative skills and writing at length.
In religion, children will learn about and learn from the different kinds of questions human beings can ask about religious origins, beliefs and practices, namely questions that derive from philosophy, theology, social sciences and history.

A Primary Trust for Primary Schools
PE
At Ewell Grove, we are an active school dedicated to inspiring all children to embrace healthy lifestyles. Our engaging, challenging, and fun-filled sports and activities keep children physically active for sustained periods. We pride ourselves on creating an inclusive environment where Physical Education (PE) is adaptable and enjoyable, allowing every child to thrive and enhance their physical abilities.
Our progressive curriculum is thoughtfully sequenced to ensure a clear progression of skills, interwoven through dance, gymnastics, athletics, team sports, outdoor adventure, and swimming. From the very beginning, we focus on developing fundamental skills such as balance, agility, coordination, and core strength. By encouraging larger muscle movements, we lay a solid foundation for fine motor control and hand-eye coordination, which are the key skills that support early literacy development.
Children gain a secure understanding of how their bodies function and learn the vital role exercise plays in overall health and well-being. Our core sports values of friendship, equality, respect, determination, courage, and excellence are embedded throughout the curriculum and form our whole school ethos. Through a variety of extracurricular sports activities and competitive events with local schools and across the Lumen Learning Trust, we promote not only physical development but also positive mental well-being. These experiences encourage teamwork and leadership skills, bringing joy and a sense of achievement to our children.
At Ewell Grove, we adopt a model, practice, apply approach that emphasises the Characteristics of Effective Learning. Children engage in play and exploration through open-ended activities as well as feeling motivated to take risks and embrace new challenges in an environment that encourages creativity and critical thinking.
Our inspirational sports coach collaborates closely with teachers and teaching assistants to meet the diverse needs of our children through adapted group teaching. We provide targeted support to reduce barriers within our Physifun sessions, ensuring a flexible approach that supports individual needs. Fundamental movement skills are developed through dance, gymnastics, personal challenges, and team games.
In competitive games, children work collaboratively, applying principles of attack and defence while ensuring our sports values of teamwork and social interaction. Each year culminates in the Ewell Grove Games, a celebration that includes every child and showcases their achievements while promoting the significance of leading active lifestyles. In Key Stage 2, children have the opportunity to apply foundational skills during outdoor adventure experiences. Swimming lessons begin in Year 4, allowing children to practice and refine fundamental skills, ensuring they leave Ewell Grove as competent swimmers.
Children at Ewell Grove develop a strong sense of belonging and community through teamwork, competition, inclusive whole-school events, and the celebration of their achievements. Events like the Ewell Grove Games instil a rich sense of tradition and community spirit. Every child is empowered to achieve and excel, regardless of their starting point.
Throughout their time at Ewell Grove, children consolidate a range of skills, including performance evaluations and personal best comparisons. Independence, confidence, and resilience flourish as children learn to overcome challenges and recognise their successes in various physical activities. They gain a deep understanding of the importance of exercise and health, fostering lifelong fitness habits closely linked to personal, social, and emotional well-being. We ensure that every child leaves Ewell Grove with lasting memories, essential skills, and values that prepare them for future endeavours, setting them on a path toward a healthy and active life.
